text:
Dear Dr Ainsley

Re: emphysema in a 36 year old.

She was referred after a CT thorax done for persistent cough showed basal panlobular emphysema.
Alpha-1 antitrypsin level 0.6 g/L, phenotype PiZZ. That explains it.

Spirometry: FEV1 2.14 L (68%), FEV1/FVC 0.61, no significant reversibility.

Twenty pack year history, stopped in March 2024 and has stayed stopped.

She has never been admitted with a respiratory infection and has had no exacerbations requiring
steroids in the last twelve months.

Her brother has also been found to be PiZZ and is under the Newcastle service.

We would consider augmentation therapy if the FEV1 declines faster than 60 mL per year, which is
not the case at present.

Vaccinations up to date. Pulmonary rehabilitation referral made.

Yours sincerely
Dr K. Prasad

Cough again, 10 days, productive, no fever.

Chest: scattered wheeze, no focal signs. Sats 97%. Afebrile.

Acute bronchitis on a background of emphysema. Doxycycline 200 mg then 100 mg for 4 days.

The miscarriage in 2018 came up again today. She is fine talking about it but wanted it recorded
that she does not want it raised at every appointment. Noted.

Tubal ligation 2021, so no contraception needed.

Review if not settling in a week, or sooner if she becomes breathless at rest.
